answer.evidence: The sample is a repeating pattern of dark green foliage clumps with pink highlights, in a block with a bump on top. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The scalloped rim at rows 16-19 is only the silhouette outline. The column scans show the same light/dark cycle every 16 rows (e.g. x=64 rows 15-22, 31-38, 47-54) that repeats the tile pattern, not a top surface. Width goes 35 to 65 to 85 to 96 at rows 16-19, which is a rounded silhouette edge and not a lid. No contents are visible. This is a flat tiled texture seen face-on and reads as a front elevation without a top plane.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a canopy autotile block, and its scalloped top edge and dithered dark mass do read as foliage. But it has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per 16x16 tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The main canopy ramp has about 3 lightness steps: a deep dark green-black base, a mid dark green, and a few pink-mauve highlight clumps. The references have 5-6 greens with per-clump highlights and shadows. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint and counts as dark_material_tone. Flat-fill coverage is 0% thanks to the dithering, which gives some texture, but the pink spots are sparse and uniform and do not build leaf clumps one by one. Overall it is far shallower and flatter than the references, and the large gap in colour count and density means it fails.
